{{Short description|British chemist (1924–2021)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Roy McWeeny''' (19 May 1924 – 29 April 2021) was a British academic physicist and chemist.

McWeeny was born in [[Bradford]], [[Yorkshire]] in May 1924. His first degree was in physics from the [[University of Leeds]]. He then obtained a D.Phil. in [[mathematical physics]] and quantum theory under the supervision of [[Charles Coulson]] at the [[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford]].

From 1948 to 1957 he was lecturer in [[physical chemistry]] at King's College, [[Durham University|University of Durham]] (King's College is now the [[University of Newcastle upon Tyne]]). From 1957 to 1965 he was at the [[Keele University|University of Keele]] rising to Professor of [[Theoretical Physics]] and [[theoretical chemistry|Theoretical Chemistry]]. From 1966 to 1982 he was Professor of [[theoretical chemistry|Theoretical Chemistry]] at the [[University of Sheffield]]. In 1982 he moved to the [[University of Pisa]], [[Italy]] where he remained an [[Emeritus Professor]] until his death.

In 1996 a celebratory ''festschrift'' volume was published in his honour containing original
papers by 132 scientists from 19 countries.<ref>[[International Journal of Quantum Chemistry]], {1996}, Volume 60, No 1.</ref> He was awarded the 2006 Spiers Memorial Medal by the Faraday Division of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] and the Medal Lecture, "Quantum chemistry: The first seventy years", was  published in [[Faraday Discussions]].<ref>Faraday Discussions, 135, 13 - 30, (2007), ''Chemical Concepts from Quantum Mechanics'', ISSN 1359-6640</ref><ref>[http://www.rsc.org/publishing/journals/FD/article.asp?doi=b615518a Abstract of Albert Spiers lecture]</ref> He has served on the editorial board of [[Molecular Physics (journal)|Molecular Physics]], [[Chemical Physics Letters]] and [[International Journal of Quantum Chemistry]].

He has written many scientific papers and seven books, of which perhaps the best known are ''Coulson's Valence'' in 1979, an update of the famous book by [[Charles Coulson]] originally written in 1951, and the two editions of ''Methods of Molecular Quantum Mechanics'', (the first edition with B. T. Sutcliffe in 1969<ref>{{cite web|url=http://journals.iucr.org/b/issues/1970/09/00/a07563/a07563.pdf|author=Reviewer: Jacob Danielsen of Aarhus University|title=Review of ''Methods of Molecular Quantum Mechanics'', edited by McWeeny & Sutcliffe|website=journals.iucr.org}}</ref> and the second edition alone in 1989). He wrote several chapters in the three volumes of the ''Handbook of Molecular Physics and Quantum Chemistry''.<ref>Published by Wiley, Chichester, 2003.</ref> In 1963 he wrote ''Symmetry: an introduction to group theory and its applications''.<ref>Published by Pergamon Press, 1963.</ref>

From 2002 he edited an open-access series of [http://www.learndev.org/ScienceWorkBooks.html Basic Books in Science], several of which he authored himself. He was also an elected member of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]] and the  [[European Academy of Arts, Sciences and the Humanities]].

McWeeny died in [[Pisa]], [[Italy]] in April 2021 at the age of 96.<ref>[https://www.unipi.it/index.php/news/item/20943-ateneo-in-lutto-per-la-scomparsa-del-professor-roy-mcweeny Ateneo in lutto per la scomparsa del professor Roy Mcweeny]</ref>
